To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ca(2+) responses of single platelets immobilized on fibrillar substrates are different from those in suspensions of the cells.

the initiation of repetitive spiking in single, fibrin-ogen-bound platelets is due to stimulation of the phospholipase pathway, whereas the slow oscillations of [Ca2+], evoked by the inhibition of the Ca2+ pump, are due to Ca2+-induced Ca2+-release.

in single platelets the Ca(2+) signal evoked by ADP and thrombin is characterized by rapid spiking and a slow phase of oscillations, whereas in the absence of agonists the signal is characterized by slow oscillations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the spiking of [Ca2+].
the role of Ca2+ in platelet activation.
a mechanism of Ca2+-induced Ca2+-release and the role of the TG-sensitive Ca2+ pool in the Ca2+-signaling of platelets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in platelets there are two pools of Ca2+, one of which is sensitive to TG and the other is insensitive to this drug.
the platelet calcium responses are very sensitive to the presence of fibrinogen and to the concentration of thrombin.
the Ca(2+) responses of single platelets are more complex than the responses of platelets in suspension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+ response of platelets to TG is a complex process, which is modulated by the Ca2+ level and the activity of phospholipases C and A2.
Ca2+ oscillations in single, adherent platelets involve a complex interplay of Ca2+ release mechanisms, Ca(2+)/calmodulin-dependent phosphatases, and Ca(2+)/CaM-dependent kinases.

the spiking and plateau responses of [Ca2+](i) are due to the activation of the PLC-Ca(2+) pathway, whereas the slow oscillations are due to the inhibition of Ca2+ pumps and the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium response of platelets to thrombin is biphasic: an initial phase of spiking followed by a plateau of elevated [Ca2+] i.
Ca2+ responses in single platelets are different from those in suspensions of the same cells and that the responses of single platelets are more complex than previously believed.
the calcium responses of single platelets can be used as a tool to probe the mechanisms of intracellular calcium regulation in platelets and other cells.
